title: Firefighter Cancer Registry Act of 2018
official_summary:
Firefighter Cancer Registry Act of 2018

(Sec. 2) This bill requires the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) to develop and maintain a voluntary registry of firefighters in order to collect history and occupational information that can be used to determine the incidence of cancer among firefighters. The registry must be used to improve monitoring of cancer among firefighters and to collect and publish epidemiological information. The CDC should seek to include specified information in the registry, including the number and type of fire incidents attended by an individual.

To collect information for the registry, the CDC must enable the registry to connect to state-based cancer registries.

The CDC must also: (1) develop a strategy to encourage participation in the registry, (2) develop guidance for states and firefighting agencies regarding the registry, and (3) seek feedback on the registry from nonfederal experts.

The CDC must make registry data available to the public and in accordance with privacy laws.

summary.headline: Requires the CDC to set up a voluntary national registry tracking cancer among firefighters.
summary.what_it_does: The law directs the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention to create and maintain a voluntary registry of firefighters. The registry collects work history and job information, such as the number and types of fire incidents a person responded to, so that cancer rates among firefighters can be tracked and studied. The CDC must link the registry to state cancer registries, encourage participation, give guidance to states and fire agencies, and publish data in line with privacy laws.

who_it_affects.how: Firefighters may choose to join the voluntary registry and share their work history and incident information.
State cancer registries are expected to connect with the federal firefighter registry to help collect information.
Agencies receive CDC guidance on the registry and may be asked to help encourage firefighter participation.
States receive CDC guidance on the registry and must work with it through their cancer registries.
